claims.text: A technical strategy is a short document naming the main challenge a system faces, the direction chosen to meet it and the few actions that follow, for a stated period.

claims.text: technical-strategy.md: period one year from Sprint 23 (assumed); written by the team lead with the product owner; it does not decide again the ADRs it points to, it shows them as parts of one plan.

Diagnosis: one shop to 1,000 (assumed, three years); weak points: no row knows its shop, no Prometheus in production so slo.md SLOs are unmeasured there, backups and WAL do not yet leave the database machine, one team where 1,000 shops need three to four.

Direction: one shared deployment (ADR 0012), every shop's data in shared tables with shop_id and row-level security (ADR 0013), on one provider's managed Kubernetes (ADR 0022); opening a shop adds data, not a copy of the system.
A shared deployment means a bad release reaches every shop, so small api changes go through canary and shop-visible changes sit behind a feature flag (ADR 0019).

Not-doing: no more services (ADR 0012); no mesh (ADR 0021: fills two gaps nobody asked for, cost at every Pod and call); no second cloud (ADR 0022: doubles the platform; exit plan holds the risk of being tied to one provider); no rewrite (source: Caddyfile, httproutes.yaml).
The 'no rewrite' row describes a strangler fig without using that name.

Six actions H1-H6, each with an owner role and a document; H1 points to multi-shop-data-rollout.md (three releases); H3 names Prometheus; H4 copies backups to a second region, an area of the same infrastructure provider.
claims.source_hint: docs/team/technical-strategy.md @ stage-4 lines 45-52; docs/design/multi-shop-data-rollout.md Release 1-3 headings; docs/adr/0020 lines 10-13

claims.text: The file says a strategy without actions is only a wish, and order and timing of actions live in roadmap.md.

Review: every quarter, with roadmap.md and the 'Giả định cần theo dõi' table of architecture-governance.md; if the diagnosis changes (e.g. a contract demands a separate copy of the system) the strategy is rewritten first, then the roadmap.
An accepted ADR is not rewritten; a changed decision is recorded in a new ADR and the old one only changes status to superseded.
The not-doing list saves the team from deciding the same ideas again; an idea never turned down tends to return at every review.

Trade-offs: a strategy fits when one challenge outgrows any single decision, and alone puts every ruled-out idea in one place tied to the diagnosis; a tool list names tools, not problems; ADRs alone suffice with no large shared challenge; a vision without actions changes no work.

Recommended rule, not written in Đơn Hàng's files: an idea that serves no action and is not on the not-doing list waits for the next review unless shown to answer the diagnosis; with one shop and no large change, ADRs one at a time may be enough.
